figures.finding: No permit or licence exists for a child performer: the general labour law reaches performing work as it does any other. No one may employ a child under twelve in any occupation whatever, save light domestic or farm work at home; under fourteen a child may not work in an agricultural or industrial undertaking, which includes a commercial enterprise of any kind, save family undertakings, youth-organisation fund-raising or beside adult relatives, and then outside school hours, at most eight hours a day and thirty a week and never at night; a young person (fourteen to eighteen) needs a medical examination first, may not work in school hours while of school age, and not at night (10 p.m. to 5 a.m.) in an undertaking. Nothing in either Act distinguishes acting from writing or directing: any of them done as employment is caught, a freelance commission is not (reading).

sources.said: "child" means a person who in the opinion of the Court, in a prosecution for an offence against this Act, is under the age of twelve years; ... in any occupation whatsoever any child:

"child" means a person under the age of fourteen years; ... "industrial undertaking" means any manufacturing, mining, storage, construction, or land, sea, or air transport enterprise; and the term includes a commercial enterprise of any kind and any office or other related operation; "night work" means work performed between the hours of ten p.m. and five a.m.; ... E3. (1) No child shall be employed or shall work in ... a public or private agricultural or industrial undertaking or ... in any branch thereof, or on any ship: ... Provided further that any chid so working shall not work ... within school hours or for a period of more than eight hours ... in any twenty-four hour period or more than thirty hours ... in any one hundred and sixty-eight hour period or at night. ... E5. (1) No young person shall be employed unless ... he has been found fit for the work he is expected to perform ... after a thorough medical examination; ... (2) A person shall not employ a young person who is ... within the compulsory school age during school hours.

figures.finding: No one under eighteen may form or join in forming a company, and anyone so barred may not be a company's director.
figures.applies: Companies Act 1995 (No. 18 of 1995), ss. 4(2) and 66(1); amendments to 2025 listed on laws.gov.ag were not compared.
